record.paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
record.original_question: For a prime homogeneous ideal P contained in (x1,...,xn)^2 in S = k[x1,...,xn], is the largest degree of an element in a minimal homogeneous generating set of P at most deg(S/P)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field and $S = k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ be the standard graded polynomial ring with $\deg(x_i)=1$. Let $P \subset S$ be a homogeneous prime ideal contained in $(x_1,\dots,x_n)^2$ (i.e., $P$ is nondegenerate in the sense that it has no linear generators and, after a suitable embedding, contains no linear form). For a minimal homogeneous generating set $\{f_1,\dots,f_r\}$ of $P$, let $\mathrm{maxdeg}(P) := \max_i \deg(f_i)$, and let $\deg(S/P)$ denote the multiplicity (degree) of the graded ring $S/P$. Determine whether the inequality
$$\mathrm{maxdeg}(P) \le \deg(S/P)$$
holds for every such prime ideal $P$.
artifact.status_search_result: The Eisenbud–Goto regularity conjecture, which would have implied this generator-degree bound, was disproved by McCullough and Peeva (J. Amer. Math. Soc., 2018). Their construction yields homogeneous prime ideals $P_r$ in standard graded polynomial rings with $\mathrm{maxdeg}(P_r) \ge 3^{2^{r-1}}+1$ while $\deg(S/P_r) \le 2\cdot 6^{7r+5}$, so $\mathrm{maxdeg}(P_r) > \deg(S/P_r)$ for sufficiently large $r$. Hence the conjectured inequality fails in general.

status_evidence.title: Counterexamples to the Eisenbud–Goto regularity conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of homogeneous prime ideals P_r with maxdeg(P_r) ≥ 3^{2^{r-1}}+1 while multiplicity is at most 2·6^{7r+5}.
status_evidence.claim: McCullough and Peeva construct prime ideals violating the conjectured bound maxdeg(P) ≤ deg(S/P).

status_evidence.title: Regularity of prime ideals (McCullough–Peeva)
status_evidence.snippet: The regularity of nondegenerate homogeneous prime ideals is not bounded by any polynomial function of the degree.
status_evidence.claim: Counterexamples show no polynomial (in particular no linear) bound on maxdeg or regularity in terms of degree.
